title: Mobile rebuild is phenomenal.
body:
I love using Amazing Marvin on my computer because it has the ADHD brain as a focus. The tools that Christina and the team have developed have always made using Marvin not just productive, but also engaging. I love opening the app and using the app. I couldn’t say that about the mobile version because the computer app was so robust. 
With this update, this major overhaul, I feel the Amazing Marvin team took their time to build something that was well developed and conceptualized.
To think they were able to streamline the ux in such a natural way, it speaks volumes to their attention to detail.
Now, when I use the mobile app I’m making the same in menu and functional adjustments  or editing and selecting the most effective organization strategies, that same method and technique can be adjusted in the mobile app.
I am now able to stay inside of Marvin on my mobile device which allows me to use it as my main marvin hub.
I don’t feel limited or as if I have to be on my laptop to use the app/program effectively. Excited to continue to use the newly developed app each day.
author: Chansing2g

title: Marvin is the best!
body: I have been using Marvin for many years. It is amazing and gets better every year.

title: Best Organization App
body:
I’ve tried so many planners, task lists, and reminder apps, to help me organize, and they have never worked out for me. Amazing Marvin turned out to be just what I needed. There are so many ways to customize and setup your day depending on your preferences. If you have a lot to do, many projects, and things you need to remember - you can create a more involved system or it can be very straightforward and simple. It takes a little bit of time to get the shortcuts and strategies down. But once you do, it’s fabulous. Absolutely love this product. Thanks so much! 10/10 **The mobile app could use some updates. But overall, it works

UPDATE: Sept. 2026
The new mobile app is absolutely FANTASTIC! I was faithfully still using it all this time, but this version makes the experience so much better and accessible. I love the interface. I love Marvin’s upgrade! Well done to the team! Thanks so much for working on the app bts all this time 👏🏾👏🏾
author: N. Espo

title: Absolutely brilliant!
body: I thought the app was pretty great before, but this latest update to 1.71.0 makes the app absolutely brilliant! Everything now is more refined and easier to use, all my tasks and projects are easier to create, view, plan, schedule and track. For 25+ years I’ve been trying to find an task manager app that works like I think (I’m pretty sure I’ve downloaded, purchased, and tried every task manager on the App Store…), and this is the first time I’m completely happy with how the app functions.
author: Jiminy2025

title: New App
body: The new app is a complete game changer. If you previously used the app without using the desktop or web version and gave up on Marvin, you need to come back and try it again. I’ve used the desktop app for over a decade and just kind of accepted that the phone app would never be helpful. But now both apps work seamlessly. Shout out to the Marvin team for listening to their users and adjusting the app accordingly
author: Beccaroo321

title: Way too expensive
body: I really wish I could use this app, I know it would solve so many problems for me and truly be useful but unfortunately it’s insanely and prohibitively expensive. I’ve had many, many productivity app subscriptions but have almost never seen one like this at literally almost 3x the usual cost.
author: Finfamx4

title: Not low executive function friendly
body: This did not feel ADHD friendly at all. I tried to put in tasks but they disappeared and couldn’t put in energy level etc. cool concept but user interface is not ideal for new users who want something low effort
author: mermerr

title: Outstanding Customer Service - Thank You Branko!
body:
Amazing Marvin is incredible! So customizable and creative. I've used a lot of habit/to-do list software and settled on Notion for a few years, but I kept running into certain points of friction. So far, it seems like Marvin can solve them! It takes time to set up and all the features can be overwhelming, but it's worth it for the customizability. 

The team is extraordinarily helpful! The primary reason I took the time to write a review is that Branko in particular has given me tons of advice, replying super quickly to my questions with clear instructions that indicate a deep understanding of the product. Seems like the developers have been responsive to feature requests as well! Grateful and excited 🙌
author: Gfghvd

title: Current Version of App Is Unusable
body: As far as I remember this is my only 1-star review. I can open the app once, and log in. After initial log in the app locks on the start animation and then crashed. Support suggested I use the web app. I have tried it but the tiny touch points are annoying. I like the service but mobile is key part of my workflow and this just does not work. Back to Todoist for me.
author: Wilsongis

title: Great
body: It can be simple or super custom.
author: 123abcyouand me

title: Calendar sync is a joke
body:
Wasted 3.5 hours of hyper focus trying to get the calendar sync to either display all the items at once, or not duplicate them times 5. 

Customer service never wrote back when I asked about student discount.

Zero percent chance I’m paying that much for some broken (cr)app.

For an app that’s supposed to reduce adhd stress, I am livid and near tears. 

*adult word* YOU
author: MercreatureRyn

title: The best app out there
body: I know the mobile app is a little behind the desktop app, but there is no app out there quite like Amazing Marvin. Grateful for it every day!
author: Jpbd97547

title: Great App! Wish there was more development on ios apps
body: I have ADHD and this was the app that finally got me motivated for all of my to dos. The customization is just right, not overwhelming or underwhelming and very user friendly. Only downside is that I hate how this looks on the IPad and that’s were I prefer to do a bulk of my planning and work, and many features are difficult or impossible to access on the IPad.
author: roohafzamilk

title: The one app to rule them all
body: I’ve tried every task / productivity app out there, I have ADHD, so eventually I’ll get bored & stop using them. But AM is so customizable,  that when I feel I start to get bored, I can change my flow or strategy & it feels like a brand new app. No other app is capable of doing this. The bad reviews of the phone app are unfair in my opinion, because yes, the phone up can’t compare to the Mac or web apps, but is not supposed to, is meant to be a companion app, it does all the most important stuff & then some more. If you’re one of those who changes apps all the time because you either get bored or because you can’t find one that has everything you need in a productivity app, try AM. It can be a little overwhelming at first due to being SO customizable, but don’t get discouraged, their video tutorials are a lot of help, and so are their Subreddit & Facebook group. Customer service is A+
author: MalloryKnoxxxx

title: Amazing app for getting things done
body:
I’ve tried a bunch of different apps (Todoist, Things 3, Clickup, Trello, and more) and am surprised Amazing Marvin isn’t getting more attention! It works great out of the box, and there are lots of helpful features you can add on depending on what works for you.

What I value is that unlike other apps that mainly just focus on to do list maintenance, Amazing Marvin has tools to help you plan and manage your time in a flexible way - for example, you can set up time blocks and add tasks to them. Highly recommended for people who could use some help with actually getting things done!
author: Jenny10954

title: LOVE LOVE LOVE
body: I love amazing Marvin. I have been stuck in a lot lately. In fact, I think I’ve always been stuck in a rut. I have tried many organizing systems, whether they are in the physical form or in the digital form but none has ever stuck. That is where  amazing Marvin comes into play, I love how amazing Marvin has all the options out there in one compact place and all you have to do is set the settings to work with the tools that work best with you or the fact that you can have fun experimenting. My favorite feature has to be the self-control, the procrastinator doctor, and the goals, and projects features.
author: keikokomikokoi

title: The product is great - the app is lacking
body:
The title says how I feel. Amazing Marvin is worth it if you’re going to use it for work and computer based projects and tasks. 
For me, I use my task manager for everything from work to home to the boards I’m on to my role in church and with ADHD I’ve started adding every little thing… “make sure the kids are breathing” - ✅. 

I need an app on the go with me. This ain't it.
author: leelpatt

title: Will there be an iPad update?
body: I get that the backend customization may be web only but once it’s built it’d be nice for the iPad to have the full screen & not just reduced to the phone format
author: be.muriel

title: Was good while it lasted
body: No updates in a long time, moving on.
author: Brandon3003

title: No update in over 1 year
body:
The app hasn’t been updated in over 1 year. Not a good sign. 

Try Things 3 instead.
author: Seriously, man?

title: Lots of potential
body:
If my focus was my personal productivity, I’d be all over this app. The way they approach productivity is novel and the flexibility of the design is appealing. 

However, keeping things in line professionally is a much larger concern, and this app lacks out-of-the-box integrations with the tools I use at work.

I really wanted to dig in and do more, but can’t justify double-entry or spending the time setting up two-way sync with something like Zapier or Power Automate.
author: NicknameNotTakenMaybe

title: Seriously the best!
body: The mobile app isn’t full featured yet, and I wish it had some additional functionality sometimes. BUT, otherwise Marvin is the most amazing task and project manager ever. I’ve used Todoist, Things, apple reminders (still use for things like groceries), bullet journal/paper lists and other programs like Obsidian or Evernote for more of the project management side. It’s not the slickest out there, but Marvin beats them all and makes me want to plan projects out and helps me beat procrastination and improve focus - especially for large long term projects. It’s got so much amazing functionality and ways to organize. Plus a great community and serious developers. Highly recommend!!
author: ER 111

title: Total Waste of Time
body: Obscure competitor of several similar and better apps. Nothing is clear until you watch the videos and learn what the icons do. In contrast to Things, for example, where you barely have to think at all.
author: uinazi

title: Best to do app ever
body: I love how everything is configurable, so you can change how you organize your task list at will or try out new strategies like time blocking or the Eisenhower matrix. I’ve tried many apps to organize myself, but this is the only app I’ve been able to replicate what I do when I organize my tasks on paper. I have brain injury, so it’s been hard to keep organized, but this has helped me keep track of everything. I can even print out my to do list as a backup or to tape my urgent tasks to my physical calandra. The phone app isn’t as useable as the desktop app, but has improved quite a bit since the earlier versions. If you like to customize everything, this is awesome. I’ve used Todoist, Asana, Trello, and many others, but they all basically have only one way of doing things, which is very limiting, but this allows you to do all those things and more.
author: Galadien

title: Love Marvin, but the App Woefully Behind!
body:
As a concept, Marvin truly is amazing! The incredible variety of “strategies” alone is brilliant, allowing for endless task and time-management options. And the desktop app is highly functional. So why the iOS app is soooo limited in function is baffling. 

For example, the time blocks I use to organize my work - wonderful on the desktop - are invisible on the very, very limited iOS app calendar. It’s a major strategy I use constantly, but can’t access on the go… I just don’t get it… Marvin creates these amazing tools, but makes them unreachable/unusable on the phones we use to run our lives. 

And I know that Apple limits iOS app functionality - so there is no way 1 iOS app is going to be able to accomplish all that Marvin can offer. But the iOS app still seems woefully I adequate. (Note to the Marvin team - I’d pay for the iOS app if $ is the issue!)
author: Jesusat2AM (aka Kirk Winslow)

title: Revolutionary
body: An extraordinary range of features. without parallel. The procrastination wizard is especially great.
author: Lucas2114

title: I LOVE MARVIN
body:
I absolutely love Amazing Marvin. It does an excellent job of integrating all task management strategies into a single, cohesive app. So much so that I am a lifetime subscriber.

===

===

The devs and the AM team are doing an AMAZING job. Keep up the great work everyone!!! :)

title: Stop Your Searching
body:
This is the absolute BEST organization tool. 
Please use it.

title: No iPad version

author: King KTB

title: No iPad app
body: iPhone only. Done.
author: koparosti

title: Only productivity app I’ve ever stuck with
body:
I’ve tried a large majority of the productivity apps on the market (Todoist, TickTick, Any.do, etc) as well as a paper planner, and this is the only thing I’ve been able to stick with consistently for over a year. I will say that the desktop app is where I primarily use all the great features Marvin has to offer but having a mobile version is a non-negotiable for me so Marvin is the best of both worlds. 

The ability to set schedule and due dates was key for me, and the ability to customize everything is amazing! Any time that I feel like my setup isn’t working or my task list is becoming overwhelming, I can make changes by turning strategies on and off to help me better prioritize what needs to get done. Highly recommend!!
author: rose223

title: Best Productivity Tracker
body:
Okay look, I’m not going to pretend I went 0 to 100 and magically got my life organized after using this app. I heard of Amazing Marvin after searching up productivity apps (who else has had been in a huge procrastination block from time to time?). 

You get a one month free trial before you commit, which I find more than generous. At first, I signed up and probably spent a good few days looking at the different workflows and strategies (they have helpful videos) and checking and unchecking them to see what suited me. I can’t say I’m totally on this the whole time and rid of all my procrastination habits, but this really helps and I love the dancing Marvin when I complete something. 

This product is especially helpful on those days when I need to get things done. It incorporates events (imported from your email’s calendar!), recurring tasks, habit tracker, different strategies, etc. It’s literally on every platform so you can integrate it everywhere! It’s so flexible that if you really tinker with it you WILL find a configuration that will suit you. Sometimes it is a bit buggy, but I find it more than worth the subscription for the community, constant updates based on customer feedback (thanks to the AM team!), and flexibility. 

The ONLY thing I wish it could have was a “life homepage” or notes function where I can link all my spreadsheets somewhere (e.g. current subscriptions, budget plans, travel itineraries). 

Desktop version is way better than the app, but the app is still amazing for what it is and I am sure it will only get better from here.
author: sincerelyjackie

title: The best to-do app out there
body: Simple to get into, endless customization.
author: wyyiy

title: Great Alternative to OF3
body: I was looking for a Windows-Compatible Version to OF-3 and this was it plus with more helpful features . Still in the early stages of setting this up for myself but it has a pot of promise.
author: Silviut

title: Tons of promise, but not there yet
body:
If this app had the same functionality as the website/desktop app, it would easily be the best productivity app out there. Give it an iOS 14 widget too, and I would switch over to it from Things and happily pay the subscription. 

As it is now, it just doesn’t have the functionality I need. I’m someone who primarily runs my day from my phone, and I need a serious powerhouse app with full functionality to do that.
author: Sundayraven

title: This is it.
body:
This app is the end all be all for me. I used to bounce between productivity apps because each of them had something I liked but I always had to pick and choose. Not anymore, this one has truly everything I could need. 

I found this app because I was searching for something that would allow me to categorize my day by certain time slots that are always changing. This is the only app I have found that gives me a good way to do that. Now I can quickly add items from my todo list into these chunks of time whether they be for a meeting or just a focus block. 

This app also has incredible features to help me deal with all of the psychological hurdles to productivity like overwhelm, procrastination, time tracking and focus. 

The best part is how it’s designed so that it’s easy and simple to get started but has endless possibilities for you to add at your own pace. 

It’s so calming to open up Amazing Marvin in the morning. I finally feel like I have a handle on my days and I am so much more productive. I’ve already stuck with this app for a while and I don’t see that changing.
author: J.mino

title: App keeps crashing at startup after a week or so
body: Only solution is to uninstall/reinstall, which removes all setting customizations. Please fix ASAP.
author: KingofTomorrows

title: Great update
body: I use marvin already more than a year and I was waiting for such improvement in the mobile app for a long time. Frankly speaking I was a bit skeptical on how authors are going to handle marvin’s vast capabilities in a mobile version. Now this update impressed me. Keep up the good work!
author: iappless

title: Not designed for tablet support
body:
The app does not support tablet screens, only showing the small phone-sized and shaped screen. It also doesn’t support horizontal screen rotation, so I really don’t think this app works for people who use their tablet as a laptop.

I really like Marvin and would like to see mobile support improve in future iterations...
author: iru38

title: Incomparable.
body: I’ve been searching for a productivity app like this for years. I’m impressed by its thoroughness, emphasis on workflow customization, and speed. Unlike almost any of the 50+ productivity apps I’ve tried over the last few years, it doesn’t feel like it’s working against you, or spying on you. Quite the contrary. And it’s available on desktops and as a web-app! For anyone serious about productivity and getting tasks done, this is the app for you.
author: ProUser9187

title: The productivity app I’ve been looking for...
body:
Marvin is fantastic. I’ve been hunting and hunting for an app that could do everything Marvin does. Plus, they have a web version and apps for all the major platforms. I love that I can take my list to any of my devices (which are more numerous than I’d like to admit). 

I love that you basically make the app what you need. It’s about as customizable as any app I’ve ever seen of its nature. (More so on the web or desktop versions than mobile... )

It’s certainly not perfect, and there’s a bit of a learning curve. But I can tell they’ve got a wonderful concept, and that improvements will continue to come.
author: nerdexcitation

title: Great app
body: Multi platform excellent software. Sometimes to be desired in this app, but devs are responsive and making great progress with an already wonderful app.
author: Pascel

title: Amazing Marvin is quite... amazing
body: This is the first productivity app & web app system that actually gets out of your way. Every other existing product is more of a headache than the actual things you need to get done. The quality and simplicity of this app is absolutely stunning.
author: Russ Atherton

title: Excellent platform, but the app is sorely lacking
body:
I use Marvin every day to manage work tasks, household chores, personal projects, etc. It's fantastic—the customizability via enabling strategies makes Marvin incredibly valuable.

However, the iOS app is far behind parity with the web/desktop version. Syncing takes several minutes, few strategies are enabled, the interface is clunky, and it's never updates. If the app worked 2/3 as well as the desktop version I'd be ecstatic but as it stands I cam barely check my daily todo list effectively on my phone.  I've just added a shortcut to the site since it's significantly more useful but the login state doesn't maintain.

To reiterate: I'd love to give this app 5 stars, Marvin is the best system I've found for managing multiple projects and tasks but the iOS app itself is barely usable.
author: manateemilitia

title: Too basic
body: The iOS app is unfortunately lacking most of the powerful functionality of the awesome web app. It wasn’t usable for me since I often have to manage my tasks/projects on mobile without having to wait to access a web/desktop app.
author: sunblush

title: Good product but needs better app functionality
body: I like the Marvin web product but the phone app is limited and there is essentially no iPad app. The iPhone won’t let me change to dark theme, won’t let me set time reminders, and has a poor interface compared to web product.  The iPad app is a bigger version of the iPhone app and won’t work on its side with a keyboard.  For a paid platform, app development should be better.  Really disappointed.
author: Snarkymeister

title: Perfection!
body: This is the productivity app I have been searching for! I have tried them all and nothing else has all the productivity tools that Amazing Marvin has wrapped into one. Not only do you create to-do lists in an organized manner but you can also schedule those tasks so they don’t just sit in a list getting stale. It provides tons of ways to help you become more efficient with strategies like “eat the frog”, time-blocking, labels and lots more. With so many choices on how to organize my tasks, I can customize my experience to best fit how my brain works. I’m in LOVE!
author: Me1981111

title: Compatibility Mode
body: The app does not fully support iPhone 7 Plus and I’m guessing newer phones. There’s also ugly visual artifacts.
